name: Precomputed Multi-resolution Mesh Generation
summary: Generates Neuroglancer precomputed 3D meshes, with optional multi-resolution levels of detail, from a precomputed segmentation volume using igneous.
description: Runs igneous meshing tasks on a local precomputed segmentation layer, then a merge pass that writes either single-resolution mesh manifests or unsharded multi-resolution meshes (when nlod > 0). Use it to make segmentation objects viewable as surfaces in Neuroglancer. The input must be a precomputed segmentation layer (the code reads <layer>/segmentation); the processed layer directory is moved into the output directory. The cloudpath parameter is not read: the path is always derived from the input.

inputs.description: Neuroglancer precomputed segmentation layer; the code meshes the 'segmentation' subdirectory of the input.

outputs.description: The precomputed layer directory with the generated mesh fragments and mesh manifests (or multi-resolution meshes).

parameters.description: Not read by the code; the layer path is always built from the input as file://<layer>/segmentation.
Local directory into which the processed layer (with meshes) is moved.
Resolution level (mip) of the segmentation at which meshes are generated.
Size in voxels (x y z) of each meshing task, as three space- or comma-separated integers.
Intended to toggle quadratic edge-collapse mesh simplification; the code reads the key 'simplification' (no trailing space), so this setting is not applied and simplification stays on.
Skip objects smaller than this many voxels; empty means no filtering.
Optional list of label IDs (comma- or space-separated) to mesh; empty meshes all labels.
Fill missing chunks with zeros instead of raising an error.
Mesh encoding passed to igneous ('precomputed' or 'draco').
Show a progress bar during meshing.
Generate a spatial index for bounding-box queries.
Generate shard fragments for a later sharded format.
Magnitude for the manifest/merge pass, controlling index granularity.
Run igneous tasks in parallel on all cores (true) or single-threaded (false).
Number of extra levels of detail; values above 0 create multi-resolution meshes, 0 writes single-resolution manifests.
Vertex quantization bits for multi-resolution meshes.
Minimum chunk size (x y z) for multi-resolution meshes.
